newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch bourse and FTSE Intl launch European Footsie.
newsitem.headline: Dutch bourse and FTSE Intl launch European Footsie.

text.p: Amsterdam Exchanges (AEX) and financial indices compiler FTSE International said on Thursday they had joined forces to revamp Amsterdam's Eurotop 100 index and launch a new, broader-based FTSE Eurotop 300 index.

Under the deal, FTSE International will take over the calculation of the Eurotop 100, which has been recompiled in line with commonly-accepted industry criteria and renamed the FTSE Eurotop 100 index. In addition FTSE International, a 50-50 joint venture between Britain's Financial Times and the London Stock Exchange, will launch a new, broader-based index of Europe's top 300 companies in terms of market capitalisation.
"These products will become the European standard for hedging equities exposures," AEX chairman George Moeller told a news conference.

He said AEX, created on January 1 through the merger of Amsterdam's stock and options exchanges, has exclusive rights to trade options on the index and its new FTSE Eurotop 300 counterpart in the European time zone.

FTSE International's Alistair Herbert said a European partner exchange to list futures on the two indices was still being sought, adding "We are currently in talks with LIFFE (London International Financial Futures Exchange) on this."
AEX currently lists futures on the Eurotop 100, but contract volumes were negligible, Moeller said.
The FTSE Eurotop 100 is a liquid, fixed-basket index comprising the 100 most-traded stocks in nine European countries and covering around 40 percent of the European market.
Unlike its predecessor, the FTSE Eurotop 100 is not subject to a limit on country weight, while component stocks are now weighted according to market capitalisation rather than trading volume.

Another change is that the new 100 index will be denominated in guilders rather than ECU. According to a spokesman, experience with Eurotop futures on NYMEX in New York showed investors preferred local currency listings.
Market makers in the revamped index are Optiver, Target Traders and Timber Hill (Europe) AG.
Together they will hold firm for at least 45 options and 20 futures, Timber Hill's general manager in Germany Robert Prior said, adding "there will always be deep and liquid markets."
The new FTSE Eurotop 300 is set to go live in July, Herbert said.

A compilation of Europe's 300 largest companies by value in 13 national markets, it offered 65 percent coverage of the total European market and could be used to replace composite national indices, Herbert said.

Unlike its 100 counterpart, which is a fixed basket for a year, the FTSE Eurotop 300 would change along with the market, taking into account new issues and other developments as they occurred, he said.
The Eurotop 300 would also incorporate three sub-indices, representing the Euro bloc of core EMU countries, Europe excluding the United Kingdom and Economic Groups, Herbert said.
Moeller said the new indices would help Amsterdam Exchanges in its drive to rank among the top bourses in a border-free Europe.
"There is no doubt we will survive the advent of a single currency," he said.

"We want to be the top exchange in Dutch securities but we are also looking to provide one or two or three very attractive international products, making us one of the most important European exchanges with the advent of a single market," he said.
Several more projects were in the pipeline to be announced later this year, Moeller added.
